title: An Enforcement Foundation for Constrained Equal Awards
abstract: arXiv:2611.26247v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Standard claims problems take claims as given. We ask how rule selection changes when a certified claim can be augmented by a privately known component that is costly to verify. In a binary environment, equal treatment of equals, claim boundedness, and efficiency impose a sharp lower bound on the gain from exaggeration and hence on the expected auditing needed for truthful reporting to be weakly dominant. The constrained equal awards (CEA) rule attains this bound at every report profile through a correlated audit policy. Conversely, every profilewise audit-minimal rule is CEA. The pointwise result also makes CEA the unique admissible rule that minimizes expected verification cost under every prior over true claims.

translated_title: 约束等额分配规则的执行基础
translated_abstract: 标准的索赔问题将索赔额视为给定。我们研究当经认证的索赔额可以通过一个私人知情且验证成本高昂的成分加以扩充时，规则选择会发生怎样的变化。在一个二元环境中，同等待遇、索赔有界性和效率对夸大索赔的收益施加了一个严格的下界，从而使真实报告成为弱占优策略所需的预期审计量也随之有了下界。约束等额分配（CEA）规则通过一种关联审计策略，在每一个报告组合处都达到这一下界。反之，每一个逐组合审计量最小的规则都是CEA规则。这一逐点结果还使CEA成为在真实索赔的任意先验分布下都能最小化预期验证成本的唯一可容许规则。
tldr: 本文证明在索赔额可被夸大且审计成本高昂的环境中，约束等额分配（CEA）规则是唯一能在任意报告组合和任意先验分布下最小化预期审计成本、并使真实报告成为弱占优策略的公平分配规则。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that in environments where claims can be exaggerated and verification is costly, the constrained equal awards (CEA) rule is uniquely audit-minimal—attaining a sharp lower bound on expected auditing at every report profile and under every prior, thereby making truthful reporting weakly dominant.
